question: What will be the Freddie Mac 30-year fixed mortgage rate for the week ending 2026-08-27, as first published?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the first published value of the Freddie Mac 30-year fixed mortgage rate for the week ending 2026-08-27 (FRED series MORTGAGE30US). Later revisions are ignored.
research:
# Research brief: Freddie Mac 30-year fixed rate (MORTGAGE30US), week ending 2026-08-27

## 1. Resolution source
- FRED series MORTGAGE30US mirrors Freddie Mac's weekly Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS), which is released on Thursdays. Every attempt to fetch FRED, the Freddie Mac archive and the news pages was refused by the proxy, so the values below come from search-result summaries of Freddie Mac releases.
- 2026-08-20: The latest release shows the 30-year fixed at **6.65%**, down from 6.67% the week before. The 15-year was 5.95%, and the 30-year was 6.58% a year earlier. Freddie Mac's chief economist Sam Khater said a dip in rates gave buyers "modest relief" and made shopping around worthwhile. [Freddie Mac PDF](https://freddiemac.gcs-web.com/node/31981/pdf), [Compliance Alliance](https://compliancealliance.com/news-events/entry/mortgage-rates-decline-for-second-consecutive-week/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The value will be published on Thursday 2026-08-27. PMMS mostly reflects applications submitted between Thursday and Wednesday, so the window is roughly Aug 20 to Aug 26.
- The current print is 6.65%, inside the question's range of 6.25 to 7.05 and about 40 bp from either end.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-19: Mortgage News Daily (MND) put its daily 30-year index at 6.72%, down 3 bp, citing lower oil prices and a change to the Treasury's bond buyback program. MND runs about 5 to 7 bp above Freddie Mac. Other daily surveys that day were mixed: Zillow via U.S. News 6.83% (up), Mortgage Research Center via Fortune 6.714%, NerdWallet "a little lower". [MND newsletter](https://www.mortgagenewsdaily.com/newsletter/n/20260819), [U.S. News](https://money.usnews.com/loans/mortgages/articles/mortgage-rates-today-august-19-2026), [NerdWallet](https://www.nerdwallet.com/mortgages/news/mortgage-rates-today-wednesday-august-19-2026), [Fortune](https://fortune.com/article/current-mortgage-rates-08-19-2026/), [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/personal-finance/mortgages/article/mortgage-and-refinance-interest-rates-today-wednesday-august-19-2026-surprisingly-calm-amid-bond-market-volatility-100000804.html)
- 2026-08-18: CNBC reported mortgage rates rising with Treasury yields. The 10-year was above 4.7% and the 30-year Treasury hit a 19-year high. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/18/mortgage-rates-treasury-bond-yields-consumer-loans.html)
- 2026-08-17: The 30-year Treasury closed at 5.31%, its highest since 2007, and eased to 5.28% on Aug 18. That day the 10-year was about 4.72% and the 2-year about 4.19%. Persistent inflation worries were cited. [thetrading.tools](https://www.thetrading.tools/chart-of-the-day/2026-08-18-30-year-treasury-highest-since-2007), [YCharts H.15](https://ycharts.com/indicators/30_year_treasury_rate_h15), [Intellectia](https://intellectia.ai/blog/treasury-yields-rising-august-2026)
- Taken together: long-term Treasury yields are near cycle highs, but the Freddie Mac rate has drifted down for two weeks.

## 4. Base rates and recent values
Recent weekly 30-year readings (Freddie Mac):
- 2026-06-25: 6.49%
- 2026-07-02: 6.43% (-6 bp)
- 2026-07-09: 6.49% (+6)
- 2026-07-16: 6.55% (+6)
- 2026-07-23: 6.58% (+3)
- 2026-07-30: 6.66% (+8)
- 2026-08-06: 6.69% (+3)
- 2026-08-13: 6.67% (-2)
- 2026-08-20: 6.65% (-2)

Sources: [Freddie Mac releases](https://freddiemac.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mortgage-rates-average-658), [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/30-year-mortgage-rate/news/569358), [Nasdaq 8/13](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/mortgage-rates-average-667-2026-08-13), [Fox Business 8/6](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/mortgage-rates-8-6-2026)

- Over these eight weeks, the weekly change ranged from 2 to 8 bp in absolute terms, with a median of about 4 to 6 bp. None exceeded 10 bp.
- The trend was a steady climb of about 26 bp from early July to a peak of 6.69% on Aug 6, followed by small declines.
- Historically, Freddie Mac weekly moves are usually within ±10 bp. Moves above 15 bp happen mainly around big data or Fed surprises.
- Both ends of the question's range sit about 40 bp from 6.65%. Reaching either one in a single week would be very unusual.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi lists a weekly market, "30-year mortgage rate this week" (ticker KX30YMORTW). I could not find the contract or prices for the week of Aug 27. [Kalshi example](https://kalshi.com/markets/kx30ymortw/30-year-mortgage-rate-this-week/kx30ymortw-26oct22)
- Kalshi's yearly "how high will the 30-year get" market: one article said it was 50-50 on going above 6.8%, written when the rate was 6.51%. Its date is not clear and it is likely stale. [The Truth About Mortgage](https://www.thetruthaboutmortgage.com/theres-apparently-only-a-50-50-chance-mortgage-rates-rise-above-6-8-this-year/)
- A Kalshi contract on any 2026 print below 5.75% was priced at 9¢ as of 2026-08-01. [simplefunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/will-any-2026-freddie-mac-primary-mortgage-market-kalshi-kxfm30ymtg-26dec31-t)
- I found no Polymarket or Manifold market and no expert point forecast for this specific week.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The survey window runs about Aug 20 to Aug 26. Daily moves in the 10-year Treasury and in MND's index over those days are the best real-time guides. Freddie Mac has recently been running about 5 to 7 bp below MND.
- The Jackson Hole symposium runs Aug 27 to 29. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's keynote is Friday Aug 28, after the survey window, though anticipation could still move yields in the days before. [regardsofwallstreet](https://www.regardsofwallstreet.com/news/jackson-hole-2026-dates-schedule-warsh-first-speech), [XTB](https://www.xtb.com/en/education/jackson-hole-2026-warsh-fed-speech)
- The next FOMC decision is Sept 16, after resolution.
- I did not check the economic data calendar for Aug 20 to 26 (jobless claims, flash PMIs, durable goods, Treasury auctions). Oil prices and Treasury buyback news were driving rates as of Aug 19.
